q: You lose 50% of your account. What gain gets you back to break-even?
why: Losses are asymmetric: after a 50% loss you need a 100% gain — loss % ÷ (1 − loss %).

q: With a 50% win rate over 100 trades, a run of 5 consecutive losses is…
why: At a 50% win rate a run of 5 losses is nearly certain over 100 trades. It is what randomness looks like, not a broken system.

q: What is the correct order for sizing a trade?
opts: Pick the lot size, then place the stop
Fix risk %, place the stop where invalidated, then derive lot size
Choose leverage, then lots, then stop
Set the target first, then the risk
why: Fix the risk amount first, place the stop where your analysis is invalidated, then calculate lot size — risk is fixed, lot size is an output.

q: For EURUSD, 1.00 standard lot: one pip (0.0001) is worth…
why: A standard forex lot is 100,000 units of base currency; for EURUSD one pip = $10 per lot.

q: 0.10 lots of gold with a $5 stop at 1:20 vs 1:500 leverage — the loss is…
opts: $50 in both cases — leverage does not set risk
why: Risk comes from lot size × stop distance only. Leverage only changes margin — same lots and stop mean the same loss at any leverage.
